rationale: Branch introduces handler unit tests for SQL dialect abstraction, but the underlying implementation has critical resource-management gaps that must be fixed before merge. Edge-case lens identified 7 blocking issues: (1) SQLAlchemy engines created in execute() are never disposed, leaking connection pools under sustained load; (2) InfluxDB clients are never closed in execute(), leaking file descriptors; (3) Engine created in error_hint() is never disposed on exception; (4) None measurement names corrupt schema dict and interpolated unsanitized into Flux queries; (5) Measurement names with quotes break Flux parsing; (6) list_tables_and_columns() crashes with AttributeError when config is None; (7) Non-SQLOperationalError exceptions escape unwrapped from healthcheck(). Test files themselves are well-structured, but they do not cover these resource-cleanup and error-path scenarios. All commits properly formatted and linting passes.

standards_review.notes: Ruff format + check both passed; no lint violations
SQLAlchemy engines and InfluxDB clients not disposed/closed in execute() and error paths
Non-SQLOperationalError exceptions escape unwrapped; missing None checks for config

findings.title: SQLAlchemy engine never disposed after execute()
findings.problem: create_db_connection() creates a brand-new SQLAlchemy Engine on every call. The returned engine is passed to handler.execute() but is never disposed afterwards — not in the success path and not in the exception path. In contrast, healthcheck() explicitly calls engine.dispose() in a finally block.
findings.impact: Each query call grows the number of live connection pools. Under sustained load or in long-running agent processes this exhausts the database server's max-connections limit. GC will eventually reclaim them, but non-deterministically.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the client lifetime in a try/finally block inside execute(). For the relational handler, call engine.dispose() in finally. For InfluxDB, call client.close() in finally. Alternatively, make create_db_connection() a context manager.

findings.title: InfluxDB client never closed in execute()
findings.problem: InfluxDBDialectHandler.execute() receives a client but never closes it. healthcheck() explicitly calls client.close() in a finally block; execute() has no equivalent cleanup.
findings.impact: Each query against InfluxDB leaves an open HTTP session. Over repeated calls this leaks file descriptors and sockets.
findings.recommendation: Have execute() or the caller wrap the client with try/finally and call client.close() in finally block.

findings.title: Engine created in error_hint() is never disposed
findings.problem: error_hint() calls create_connection() to build a new Engine but never calls engine.dispose(). If list_schema() raises, the engine leaks before the exception propagates.
findings.impact: On every query failure for a relational database, a connection pool is created and leaked. Under repeated failures this accumulates dangling pools.
findings.recommendation: Wrap with try/finally: engine = self.create_connection(config); try: schema = self.list_schema(engine, config); finally: engine.dispose().

findings.title: None measurement key silently corrupts schema dict
findings.problem: record.values.get('_value') can return None. When measurement is None, it is used as dict key and interpolated into Flux query as string 'None'.
findings.impact: Schema dict gets a None key; fields query for measurement 'None' returns empty results or error, producing incomplete schema data.
findings.recommendation: Add guard: if measurement is None: continue before using measurement.

findings.title: Measurement name unsanitized in Flux query
findings.problem: Measurement value inserted directly into f-string without escaping: measurement: "{measurement}". A measurement name containing a double quote breaks the Flux string literal.
findings.impact: If any measurement name contains a quote, list_schema() raises an exception, causing schema introspection to fail completely.
findings.recommendation: Escape double quotes: measurement.replace('"', '\\"'). Apply same fix to config.bucket in both queries.

findings.title: list_tables_and_columns() crashes on None config
findings.problem: list_tables_and_columns() calls _get_handler() with no null check for self.config. execute() guards against config is None, but list_tables_and_columns() does not.
findings.impact: Calling list_tables_and_columns() on unconfigured tool raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'dialect' instead of meaningful error.
findings.recommendation: Add guard: if self.config is None: raise ValueError(...) before calling _get_handler().

findings.title: Non-SQLOperationalError exceptions escape unwrapped
findings.problem: healthcheck() only catches SQLOperationalError. Other exceptions (gaierror, InterfaceError, ValueError) propagate as-is instead of being wrapped in ConnectionError.
findings.impact: UI sees raw exception string (e.g., '[Errno -2] Name or service not known') instead of expected 'Cannot connect to database: ...' format. Inconsistent error messages.
findings.recommendation: Add fallback: except Exception as e: raise ConnectionError(f'Cannot connect to database: {e}') from None.
